HeyMilo Labs | Remote hourly contract | Expression of interest
HeyMilo Labs is seeking U.S. real estate attorneys to review existing AI evaluation tasks against practice in their state. Your job is to decide whether an AI missed a real transaction issue, or whether the assignment, reference answer or scoring rule needs correction. We’ll confirm scope and hours when we match a matter to your state.
## What you’ll do
• Read the assignment and its source documents, then write the reference answer you would expect from an associate. Compare it with the existing answer and explain any material differences. Check the governing jurisdiction and flag missing exhibits, conflicting facts or assumptions about local closing practice.
• Compare AI-drafted work with the outcome you would accept from an associate. Identify the most consequential error and cite the agreement, exhibit or applicable authority that supports your assessment.
• Review how each task is verified. Apply its scoring rules to your reference answer and a sample AI answer. If a rule gives credit for a material omission or rejects a defensible alternative, show which answer it misjudges and propose a fix.
• Document your review so a second attorney can reproduce the score. When the file leaves a question open, identify what additional fact would resolve it.
## Example assignment
A mock purchase agreement, title commitment and survey are the basis for a buyer’s closing memo. The AI flags a recorded easement but uses the wrong deadline to object. Decide what credit the memo deserves, cite the controlling provision and revise the scoring rule so it catches the missed deadline.
## Who should apply
You hold an active U.S. law license and have personally reviewed purchase agreements, title or survey matters, commercial leases, construction contracts, real estate financing documents or closing packages in the state you identify. You can explain why an error changes the advice a client would receive. Prior AI experience is optional.
## Project workspace
You’ll complete the work independently in a virtual workspace we provide. We record only what happens on screen inside that workspace for research. Use the supplied materials and public sources. Keep client and firm files outside the workspace and complete assignments without generative AI.

Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, American Express, UnitedHealth Group, Volvo, Qualcomm, and Commonwealth Bank. Most of them came to us with the same problem: their engineers need realistic data to build and test software, and they can’t use production data to do it.
We’re looking for someone who loves to solve complex customer problems and then immediately turns around and builds a system so that this problem solves itself next time. Moreover, this person gets to the root of why and how each customer is using Tonic so that they can maximize the value every customer is getting out of our product. The ideal Solutions Architect will be proactive, coming up with creative solutions if customers aren't getting what they need, and pressing customers when they're not doing what they need to succeed.
## Why This Role, Why Now
AI has made writing code nearly free. Knowing whether that code, and the agents built on top of it, will behave in production hasn’t gotten any easier. Agents especially need realistic, messy, data to be tested against, and basic solutions / AI slop won’t surface the failures that matter. Teams are shipping faster than their test data can keep up, and that gap is our business.
The platform is robust and scalable. What makes it valuable is someone who can walk into a customer’s environment, work out where Tonic fits in their stack and their release process, prove it in a pilot, and make it stick after the deal closes. That’s this job. You’ll work alongside our AEs before the sale and with customers’ engineering teams after it, with a direct line back to our product and engineering teams.
## What You’ll Do
• Run technical discovery with prospects’ engineering, DevOps and QA teams. Map their data sources, environments and release process, and find where Tonic fits.
• Design and demo the solution, and handle the hard technical questions: security review, deployment model, performance at scale, and how Tonic fits their CI/CD.
• Scope pilots with clear, written success criteria, then run them to a decision.
• Own onboarding after the deal closes. Deploy Tonic, connect data sources, configure de-identification and subsetting, and get the customer generating usable test data within our time-to-generation targets.
• Design test-data pipelines for agent and software testing, combining de-identified production data and synthetic data to fit each customer’s environment.
• Diagnose problems as they appear: broken foreign keys, schema drift, sensitive columns missed, jobs that won’t finish. Fix them where you can. Where you can’t, understand the issue well enough to explain it clearly to the engineer who can.
• Train customer teams so they can run Tonic without you.
• Bring field insight back to product and engineering: which features matter, which bugs are blocking deals and where the product should go next.
• Support existing customers on high-complexity issues, and work with account teams to spot expansion early.
• Turn every one-off fix into something reusable: scripts, documentation, runbooks and product improvements, so each SA can support more customers than the last.
## What We’re Looking For
• A bachelor’s degree in a technical field (computer science, engineering, information systems, math or similar), or equivalent experience.
• 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Technical Customer Success or Forward Deployed Engineer.
• Hands-on experience with relational databases and data warehouses, and with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure or GCP). You can read a schema and tell quickly where the trouble will be.
• Working knowledge of how modern software gets built and tested: CI/CD, Docker and Kubernetes, test environments and testing frameworks.
• Comfort scripting and automating in Python and SQL. You’d rather build the fix than repeat the workaround.
• AI-native workflow. AI tools and agents are central to how you work. You know where they’re reliable and where they need your oversight.
• Ownership. You’ll often be the technical lead on an account, making sound calls without waiting to be told.
• Range. You can go deep with a DBA on one call and make the business case to a VP of Engineering on the next.
• Willingness to travel up to 25%, domestic and international.
## Nice to Haves
• Experience with agent evaluation and testing.
• Experience with test data management, data masking, or synthetic data tooling.
• Experience supporting security and compliance reviews in regulated industries like healthcare and financial services.
• Experience at an early-stage company or on a new product line.
## What Success Looks Like
In your first month, you’ll learn the platform and the delivery process and run pre- and post-sale engagements alongside your peers. By the end of your first quarter, you’ll run engagements on your own, and the scripts and runbooks you’ve written will have made your third onboarding faster than your first. After that, it’s about execution: converting pilots into customers and getting them live on time. You’ll also help shape how the SA function scales as we grow.
## Why Join
• You’ll be early in agent testing, a market that’s taking shape right now, working with some of the largest companies in the world.
• You’ll see an unusually wide range of technical environments, from startups to the Fortune 500 and from cloud-native stacks to mainframes.
• You’ll have a direct line from what you see in the field to what gets built.
• You’ll help define how the next generation of software and agents gets tested.
• Competitive compensation and equity.

Our browser extension layers individualized reading and writing scaffolds directly onto the digital materials schools already use, including curriculum platforms, Google Docs, websites, and PDFs. Medley is grounded in research-backed practices and is already being used by over 50 districts across the US.

We're hiring a Technical Product Manager, Pedagogy & AI Quality to ensure that Medley’s AI-powered instructional scaffolds continue to meet our high bar for quality and user experience. You'll tighten our rubrics for what high-quality scaffolds look like for reading and writing support in the areas of both multilingual learning and special education, and across various subjects. You’ll expand upon our metrics, build upon our robust evals systems, and review processes that hold our AI to that bar.
This is a hybrid role at the intersection of pedagogy and AI product work. You'll write and test prompts, label and analyze model outputs, dig through traces and error reports, and partner closely with engineering to ship quality improvements. You will also learn and leverage the research around scaffolding high-quality instructional materials for multilingual learners at different proficiency levels, as well as accommodations and supports for students with receptive and expressive language disabilities and neurodivergent students.
You'll work closely with our head of product and engineers to ensure that Medley consistently serves teachers and students in our partner districts with scaffolds that meet the highest levels of quality. • Define what "excellent" looks like. Translate research-based practice in literacy, special education, and multilingual learner instruction into clear, usable quality standards for Medley scaffolds, and set targets for AI output quality.
• Track and monitor quality with a robust evals system. Build and maintain datasets, rubrics, and eval suites and conduct regular error analysis and trace review, combining human labeling, LLM-as-judge and rule-based evals.
• Refine prompts and models as needed. Write, test, and refine prompts; run model comparisons and regression tests, making changes as needed to ensure outputs are consistently meeting target metrics and passing quality thresholds.
• Stay close to our users and represent their voice in product decisions. Regularly review signals from educators, data from support tickets, product analytics, and conduct user research with students and teachers to inform product decisions.
• Prioritize and ship AI quality and scaffold-related product improvements. Maintain a prioritized backlog of AI quality and scaffold UX issues; write clear specs, and work with engineering to scope, build and verify fixes, product updates and new features.
## What We're Looking For
• Pedagogical expertise , especially in scaffolding literacy instruction for struggling readers, special education, and/or multilingual learner education, and ideally from classroom teaching, intervention, instructional coaching or curriculum design.
• Hands-on experience with AI evals , including human labeling, LLM-as-judge rubric design, AI metrics targets definition, and error analysis of LLM outputs.
• AI product fluency : you use LLMs daily and have experience designing complex AI systems for products.
• Experience defining new features and collaborating with engineers to deliver them : you can clearly communicate a problem and solution, and work through technical tradeoffs and UX questions.
• Strong initiative, sharp judgment, and clear writing : you take action when you spot a problem, make swift decisions grounded in data and instincts, and communicate clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
## Nice to Have
• Graduate degree and/or significant direct experience in special education, reading/literacy, ESL/ELD or bilingual education.
• Familiarity with AI eval and observability tools (e.g., LangSmith, Braintrust, Arize, Langfuse) or annotation platforms.
• Proficiency in a language other than English.
• Prior work at an edtech company, or on content quality, assessment design or psychometrics.
• Familiarity with accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG) and assistive technology.
## Why Join Medley
Medley is building products for multilingual learners and students with disabilities, populations that together represent more than 20% of U.S. K-12 students and have historically been underserved by edtech.
You'll join early, work directly with founders and engineering leadership, own meaningful technical and design decisions, and help shape a product that improves access to learning for students nationwide.

We are looking for highly analytical professionals to support research and evaluation work for advanced AI and large language model (LLM) projects.
This work requires more than traditional data annotation. Contributors must be able to understand complex information, evaluate factual claims and AI-generated content, apply sound judgment, and clearly explain their decisions in English.
Depending on project needs and demonstrated skills, contributors may support **research and rubric development** or **rubric-based content evaluation**.
Previous AI or data annotation experience is helpful but not required. Strong research ability, analytical reasoning, attention to detail, and exceptional English comprehension and writing skills are more important.
**What You'll Do**
Assignments may include two closely related types of work.
**Research & Rubric Development**
In research-oriented assignments, you may:
• Research unfamiliar topics using credible and authoritative sources.
• Verify factual claims and cross-reference information across multiple sources.
• Distinguish reliable evidence from weak, unsupported, or misleading information.
• Analyze complex content and identify the criteria necessary to evaluate its quality or accuracy.
• Develop clear, objective evaluation criteria and rubrics based on research and project guidelines.
• Identify factual, reasoning, sourcing, or completeness issues in AI-generated content.
• Write clear evaluation standards that can be consistently applied by other contributors.
• Document evidence, sources, and reasoning supporting your conclusions.
This work requires particularly strong **research, synthesis, analytical writing, and authoring skills**.
**Content & LLM Evaluation**
In evaluation-oriented assignments, you may:
• Review reports, responses, or other AI-generated content against predefined rubrics.
• Evaluate factual accuracy, completeness, reasoning, relevance, and adherence to instructions.
• Apply evaluation criteria consistently across multiple tasks.
• Identify unsupported claims, inconsistencies, errors, or omissions.
• Verify information using credible sources when required.
• Assign appropriate evaluations based on established guidelines.
• Provide concise, evidence-based rationales explaining your decisions.
• Maintain consistency and attention to detail across high volumes of evaluation work.
This work places greater emphasis on **reading comprehension, judgment, consistency, attention to detail, and concise written reasoning**.
**Who We're Looking For**
Strong candidates may come from backgrounds such as:
• Research or research analysis
• Fact-checking and source verification
• Investigative or editorial research
• Journalism
• OSINT or investigative intelligence
• Due diligence or background research
• Competitive or market intelligence
• Academic or policy research
• Legal research
• Information science or library research
• Trust & Safety or content quality
• AI/LLM evaluation
• Complex data annotation or quality assurance
Candidates from other professional backgrounds are encouraged to apply if they can demonstrate the required research, reasoning, and written communication skills.
**Required Qualifications**
• **Fluent to near-native professional English proficiency (C1/C2 level or equivalent).**
• Exceptional English reading comprehension, including the ability to understand nuance, qualifiers, ambiguity, and complex written claims.
• Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.
• Ability to distinguish factual evidence from assumptions, opinions, and unsupported claims.
• Ability to produce clear, precise, grammatically strong written explanations.
• Strong attention to detail.
• Ability to follow complex written guidelines and apply them consistently.
• Ability to work independently and make evidence-based judgments.
• Strong digital literacy and online research skills.
• Ability to learn unfamiliar subject matter quickly.
English proficiency will be evaluated through a practical assessment; formal language certification is not required.
**Additional Skills for Research & Rubric Development Assignments**
Candidates considered for research and rubric-authoring work should also demonstrate:
• Advanced web research and source-verification skills.
• Ability to identify authoritative sources appropriate to a specific claim.
• Ability to synthesize information from multiple or conflicting sources.
• Ability to translate complex research findings into clear evaluation criteria.
• Strong structured writing and authoring skills.
• Ability to anticipate ambiguity and create criteria that can be consistently interpreted by other evaluators.
**Preferred Experience**
Experience in one or more of the following is beneficial:
• Fact-checking or professional source verification
• Research analysis
• Evaluation or quality review
• Rubric or guideline development
• AI/LLM evaluation or training
• Investigative research
• Content quality or Trust & Safety
• Academic, legal, policy, or market research
• Working with primary sources, government databases, academic publications, corporate records, or other authoritative sources
Previous AI experience is **not required** if you can demonstrate strong research, analytical, and evaluation capabilities.
**Assessment Process**
Qualified applicants may be invited to complete a practical online assessment.
The assessment may evaluate:
• English reading comprehension and written communication
• Analytical reasoning
• Fact-checking and source verification
• Source-quality judgment
• Evaluation of AI-generated content
• Ability to follow and consistently apply detailed criteria
• Ability to provide clear and concise rationales
Candidates being considered for research and rubric-development assignments may complete additional exercises assessing **research depth, synthesis, and rubric authoring**.
**What Success Looks Like**
Successful contributors don't simply identify whether something appears right or wrong. They can understand **why**, identify the evidence supporting that conclusion, and communicate their reasoning clearly.
For research-oriented work, this means being able to **research a topic and help define what a high-quality evaluation should measure**.
For evaluation-oriented work, this means being able to **apply established criteria accurately, consistently, and efficiently while providing a concise rationale for the decision**.

This is a **remote, project-based opportunity** supporting AI research and evaluation projects.
Project availability, workload, duration, and schedules may vary based on client requirements. Successful qualification does not guarantee a specific volume or duration of work.

At Netflix, our mission is to entertain the world. Together, we are writing the next episode - pushing the boundaries of storytelling, global fandom and making the unimaginable a reality. We are a dream team obsessed with the uncomfortable excitement of discovering what happens when you merge creativity, intuition and cutting-edge technology. Come be a part of what’s next.
We’re hiring a senior Software Engineer in Test to lead how Netflix tests the experiences members use on their TVs and phones. You’ll define what quality means for complex, fast-moving features, build the tools and automation that prove it, and help every engineer around you ship with confidence.
The Teams
Live UI
The Discovery and Viewing Experience (DVX) Live team owns the UI engineering and architecture that powers Live viewing experiences across TV, iOS, and Android. Members show up for live events once, with no second airing and no patch mid-show, so every feature we build is a promise that it will work at that moment on every device that tunes in. As our senior SDET, you’ll lead the way we test Live: recreating the moments a live event creates, like a vote opening just as an ad ends, long before the event does, so we know we’re ready instead of finding out during the show.
What we’re working on:
• The FIFA Women's World Cup, coming to Netflix in 2027 and 2031, will feature new experiences built for global, multi-match sport tournaments.
• Interactive and navigational features that help members move through a live event and catch the moments that matter.
• Real-time voting, which lets members influence a live show as it unfolds, alongside millions of others watching at the same moment.
Mobile Core
The DVX Mobile Core team develops and advances the architecture of Netflix's Android member app. We leverage systems and infrastructure widely available at Netflix and determine the best way to adopt and apply them on Android, enabling easier, more efficient patterns for downstream product engineering teams.
What we’re working on:
• Modernizing our app architecture for the iOS and Android member app. This involves driving migrations and a cross-platform Player rewrite, creating leverage for product teams to ship faster and more reliably on iOS and Android.
• Driving Quality of Experience (QoE). Owning monitoring and performance improvements across Player UI and canvases, as we scale.
The Role
Problem you’ll help solve:
• Testing and making sure millions of members see our Live-specific UI features and capabilities at the right moment, on every TV and phone.
• Giving every platform the same test plan, so TV, iOS, and Android are consistently validated the same way.
• Making tests reliable enough that PMs, designers, engineers, and our partners trust them, and fast enough to run on every change.
• Keeping quality steady while the iOS and Android apps modernize, including a cross-platform player rewrite, so faster delivery doesn’t come with more regressions.
What you’ll do:
• Lead testing for complex features across platforms. Agree on one test plan per feature that teams can trust and validate together, and implement it on TV, iOS, and Android, rather than reconciling differences afterward.
• Build automation that people trust. Evolve our test systems and CI integration across platforms so tests are fast and reliable.
• Make tricky live moments easy to test. Build ways to recreate them on demand instead of waiting for a real event, using mocks, overrides, real devices, and test data that looks like a real event and doesn’t expire.
• Make large migrations safe. Build the test strategy that lets the iOS and Android apps modernize without regressions reaching members
• Own quality metrics. Track how well we’re covered, how reliable our tests are, and which bugs reach members, and use that to decide what to improve next. That includes the client metrics that reveal problems only scale shows, and the alerts that tell us about them quickly.
• Make sure bugs only surprise us once. When a bug reaches members, make sure it comes back as a test, using agents to turn each finding into several, and document how to test each feature so the knowledge doesn’t live in one person’s head.
• Build and leverage AI tools. Act as a force multiplier to flag unwanted behaviors before they reach members, and apply agents to test authoring, failure triage, and bug analysis.
• Shape testability from the first commit. Partner with engineers on architecture and code that are easy to test, and help them write better tests themselves.
• Test where teams meet. Agree with partner teams on the contracts between our features and theirs, so end-to-end tests verify where teams meet and rehearse what members experience, rather than retesting every team’s systems.
• Collaborate beyond the team. Work with partner teams on shared test data, environments, and tools, and with teams that run live events to ensure features are ready before showtime and can be safely switched off if needed.
• Mentor and grow others, including engineers and SDETs, by reviewing test plans and test code, sharing practices, and making quality everyone’s job.
What we’re looking for:
• 8+ years of professional experience in software testing and test automation, with a strong record of leading testing for large, cross-team features or projects.
• Comfort working across platforms. You’ve tested consumer apps on more than one platform, and you’re eager to learn the platforms you haven’t used yet.
• Strong coding skills, with experience designing and building test frameworks and tools, not just writing test cases.
• Experience or strong interest in using AI for testing, such as writing tests, triaging failures, or finding gaps in coverage, with clear ways to check its results.
• Deep experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines and diagnosing flaky tests, infrastructure failures, and dependency issues.
• Experience with mocking, test data, or other ways to make hard-to-reproduce situations repeatable in tests.
• A practical, risk-based approach to quality: knowing where to invest in tests, which risks are acceptable, and when more testing isn’t the answer.
• Excellent communication and collaboration skills, including explaining quality risks and trade-offs to engineers, product managers, and partners in terms they can act on.
• Alignment with Netflix's culture and values.
Nice-to-haves:
• Experience with live streaming, video playback, ads, or other systems where split-second timing matters.
• Hands-on experience with testing frameworks on several platforms, such as Jest, Puppeteer, Espresso, or XCUITest.
• Experience driving shared testing infrastructure or quality strategies adopted by multiple teams.
• Experience testing how systems behave when things go wrong, such as chaos testing or failure drills.
Growth opportunities: We’re hiring a senior engineer, and we see this role growing into one that sets the standard for how Netflix tests its Live experiences

The Runtime team owns the programming model and engine that runs every application built on Unqork. What U’ll Do:
• Own test automation for the Runtime team. Design, write, and maintain Playwright test suites that cover critical runtime flows and run on every pull request and release. Keep them fast, deterministic, and trusted. A flaky test is a bug to fix, not a test to rerun.
• Review automation as code. Review the tests engineers write with their features, hold them to the same standard as production code, and coach the team on writing tests that catch real regressions.
• Gate releases with automation. Wire suites into CI/CD (GitHub Actions) as quality gates, track pass rate, flakiness, and run time, and decide when a release is ready to ship.

• Raise the security bar. Build checks for authentication, authorization, input handling, and data exposure into the suite, and partner with Security to turn findings into regression tests.
• Build and run performance tests. Write k6 load and stress tests for runtime APIs and rendering paths, set baselines, and catch regressions in CI before customers do.
• Use AI to scale coverage. Use Claude Code, Gemini, and similar tools to generate test scaffolding, triage failures, and grow regression coverage faster. Review their output with the rigor you'd apply to a teammate's code.
• Modernize legacy coverage. Migrate historical CodeceptJS and Selenium tests to Playwright, and retire tests that no longer earn their run time.
• Close the loop on escaped bugs. Reproduce and isolate customer-reported issues, file clear bugs with evidence and severity, and turn every escape into an automated test so it can't come back.
• Explore where automation can't. Do focused exploratory testing in the browser with DevTools, and build complex, nested applications that act like real customer use cases and push the runtime to its limits.

• Deliver a regression suite the team trusts enough to ship on.
• Find and close gaps in our test suites using client use cases, past bug patterns, and customer feedback.
• Raise the quality and security bar while increasing how fast we ship.
• Become the Runtime team's trusted voice on whether something is ready to ship.

• Strong JavaScript/TypeScript experience required. Your test code reads like production code.
• Deep, hands-on experience building and maintaining E2E suites with Playwright.
• A track record of building a stable regression suite from scratch, or turning a flaky one around, with the metrics to show it.
• Experience reviewing other engineers' test code and setting automation standards for a team.
• A solid grasp of web development: HTML, CSS, the DOM, HTTP and REST APIs, browser DevTools, and how modern front-end apps render and manage state.
• Working knowledge of web application security testing, such as the OWASP Top 10 and authentication and authorization checks.
• Experience writing performance or load tests, ideally with k6.
• Proven fluency with AI coding tools such as Claude Code, Gemini, Copilot, or Cursor, and the judgment to know when their output needs a second look.
• The ability to work autonomously as the only QA on a fast-moving team: you set priorities, make the call, and communicate risk clearly.

Job Description:
Job Title: QA Automation Analyst
Location: Remote | USA, Canada
Reports to: Team Lead, Quality Assurance
Employment Type: Full-time
## This is a new vacancy
## About the Role:
As a QA Engineer, you will own quality for features and services end to end - designing test strategy, building automation, and validating behavior across web, API, and data layers. You will partner with engineers, product managers, and other QA engineers to deliver releases that meet JD Power's quality bar.
This is a fully independent delivery role: you will take features from requirements to release-ready with minimal supervision, make sound judgment calls about risk and coverage, and contribute meaningfully to the team's automation suite and quality practices.
## In this role, you will:
• Own the test approach for assigned features; decide what to automate, what to test manually, and what to defer
• Translate requirements and acceptance criteria into complete, risk-based test coverage
• Design tests across functional, regression, integration, API, and data validation layers
• Identify gaps in requirements and edge cases during refinement, before code is written
• Assess release risk for your features and communicate it clearly
• Build and maintain automated tests independently in the team's frameworks (UI, API, and data)
• Write maintainable, well-structured test code; apply the same engineering standards expected of product code
• Integrate tests into CI/CD pipelines; keep suites fast, stable, and trustworthy
• Diagnose and fix flaky tests; drive down noise in the pipeline
• Contribute reusable utilities, fixtures, and test data helpers to the shared framework
• Investigate defects to a root-cause hypothesis before filing; include logs, traces, and reproduction steps
• Triage and prioritize defects with engineering and product partners
• Track defect trends in your area; surface patterns that point to systemic quality issues
• Verify fixes and confirm regression coverage is added where appropriate
• Partner with developers throughout the sprint; shift testing left rather than validating at the end
• Participate in code reviews and design discussions from a testability and quality perspective
• Support release activities, including smoke testing, validation, and post-release verification
• Mentor QA engineers earlier in their career on test design and tooling
• Track and report test coverage, pass rates, defect escape rate, and automation stability for your area
• Use data to argue for where testing investment should go next
• Report transparently on quality risks, blockers, and coverage gaps
## Required Qualifications:
• Post-secondary education in Computer Science or Software Engineering, or equivalent practical experience
• 5+ years developing automated tests with modern web and API frameworks such as Playwright, Pytest, Postman/Newman/Bruno/Insomnia, or REST client libraries, in TypeScript or JavaScript
• 5+ years integrating automated tests into CI/CD pipelines, with hands-on GitLab CI experience (pipeline configuration, stages, runners, artifacts, and quality gates on merge requests)
• Experience testing cloud-native services and REST APIs built on Node.js/NestJS or equivalent, including contract testing and service virtualization or mocking
• Experience validating data: writing SQL against relational databases (PostgreSQL) and cloud data platforms (Snowflake), and testing data pipelines for completeness, accuracy, and freshness
• Experience testing React front ends, including component-level testing and accessibility validation
• Experience with Git-based workflows, code review, and trunk-based or feature-branch delivery models in GitLab
• Experience with cloud infrastructure (AWS or equivalent), containerized environments, and API gateway patterns
• Experience with observability and diagnostics tooling (Datadog, or equivalent logging, metrics, and tracing platforms) to investigate failures across application, data, and infrastructure boundaries
• Detailed knowledge of all phases of the Software Testing Lifecycle, and of shift-left practices that move quality ownership into the development team
• Experience designing and executing test suites across unit, integration, contract, end-to-end, and acceptance levels, including performance and resilience testing
• Proven technical leadership of multidisciplinary teams, including distributed onshore and offshore partners
• Familiarity with service-oriented and microservice architecture, API design principles, and relational and non-relational data modeling
• Working knowledge of secure development and testing practices, including authentication and authorization flows and common application security risks
## Preferred Qualifications:
• Hands-on use of AI coding and testing assistants in daily work; experience applying LLMs to test generation, test data creation, or failure triage
• Experience building or evaluating automated quality signals for AI-enabled features — evaluation harnesses, regression suites for non-deterministic outputs, and guardrail testing
• Experience with Jira and Confluence for test management, traceability, and defect workflow
• Experience with DORA metrics and using delivery data to target quality investment

This position has a starting salary range of $80,000 - $100,000 CAD / $100,000 - $120,000 USD per year. The range represents what we reasonably and in good faith expect to pay for the role at the time of posting. An employee’s pay within the range is determined by a number of factors, including relevant skills, education, qualifications, experience, performance, business or organizational needs, and geographic location.
Eligible employees may participate in medical, dental, vision, disability, life insurance, retirement savings programs, paid time off, wellness programs, and other company-sponsored benefits. Benefits vary by country and employment status.

• Partner with our automation engineers on scenario coverage as our approach to test architecture and ownership continues to take shape

At Forbes Advisor, our mission is to help readers turn their aspirations into reality. We arm people with trusted advice and guidance so they can make informed decisions they feel confident in and get back to doing the things they care about most.
We are an experienced team of industry experts dedicated to helping readers make smart decisions and choose the right products with ease. Forbes Advisor boasts decades of experience across dozens of geographies and teams, including Content, SEO, Business Intelligence, Finance, HR, Marketing, Production, Technology and Sales. The team brings rich industry knowledge to Forbes Advisor's global coverage of consumer credit, debt, health, home improvement, banking, investing, credit cards, small business, education, insurance, loans, real estate and travel.
We pair journalism with original research: every “best of” list we publish sits on a dataset our own team has collected, scored and can defend line by line.
The Data Research and Product Testing teams own that evidence base. We decide what gets measured, how it gets weighted, and whether a claim survives scrutiny. It is the difference between an opinion piece and a recommendation a reader can act on.
About the Role
Almost every software review on the internet is written from a free trial and a marketing page. This role is the person who pays for the real tier and uses it properly.
You will run hands-on testing across a wide set of SMB and related digital products and services, signing up, using the product as a customer would, and scoring it against a written protocol. Your findings go straight into the rankings readers see. This is a role for someone already immersed in this software, not someone who intends to learn it on the way.
What you'll do
• Run hands-on tests to a written protocol and record the results in a structured, comparable form. The output is a dataset, not an opinion.
• Help design those protocols: decide what to measure, how to measure it repeatably, and what would make a result invalid.
• Own the sample pipeline for your categories: account provisioning, plan tiers, renewal dates, cancellation and offboarding.
• Document testing as you go, including screenshots and screen recordings, so the editorial team can show readers the work rather than assert it.
• Feed test scores into the Data Research scoring models, and flag loudly when a hands-on result contradicts what the marketing page claims.
• Re-test on a defined cadence so published verdicts do not quietly go stale as products and plans change.
• Write findings up clearly enough for an editor to build an article on, and stand behind them as the person who ran the test.
• Keep the testing log auditable: who tested what, when, on which version or plan tier, under what conditions.
• Write the first protocol for a category we have not tested before, and be honest in the retro about which parts of it did not survive contact with the products.
• Use AI deliberately in your day-to-day work to increase output: identify which parts of protocol drafting, test preparation, results structuring and findings write-ups it can help with, and put those techniques into practice. Demonstrate how they help you deliver more without weakening the evidence. Check the output yourself; AI-generated claims are not a substitute for hands-on test results.
Your categories
Some examples rather than the full list. This set evolves constantly, and a good deal of what you test next year is not on this page yet.
• SMB software: accounting, payroll, CRM, point of sale, website builders, HR and e-signature tools.
• Financial services journeys: banking and investing apps, budgeting apps, insurance quote flows, loan pre-qualification, tax software.
• Health-adjacent digital: telehealth, online pharmacy and therapy platforms.
• Service journeys tested by mystery shopping: identical input profiles run across multiple providers to compare quotes, onboarding and support.
About you
• Genuinely into this software. You have opinions about the app you run your own money in, you have tried more accounting, budgeting or CRM tools than anyone ever asked you to, and you can tell inside ten minutes whether a product is any good. We would far rather hire the person who already follows this market than the person who will learn to.
• A real user of these tools, not just a reviewer of them. Testing something you have never had a reason to use produces a worse review, every time.
• Fluent in the vocabulary: seat-based versus usage pricing, onboarding and activation, SSO, open banking connections, API limits, SOC 2. You should know what each of those means, which of them actually matter to a small business, and which are a checkbox on a comparison page.
• 5+ years in software QA, product testing, product support, implementation or a comparable role where you used software critically and wrote down what you found.
• Able to interrogate your own results rather than file them. The question is never only whether the test ran cleanly, it is whether it answers what editorial set out to ask. If we test payroll software and the write-up does not say what happens when a filing deadline is missed, it is worthless to an editor, and you should catch that before the cycle starts rather than after.
• An understanding that a free trial and a paid tier are different products, and that a review of one is not a review of the other.
• The discipline to keep a mystery-shopping profile consistent, so that a difference in quotes is a difference between providers and not between your inputs.
• Sharp eye for UX detail, and the vocabulary to describe why something is bad rather than just that it is.
• Organised with credentials, subscriptions and renewal dates. This role quietly accumulates a lot of accounts, and it needs doing in a way Legal is comfortable with.
• Comfortable on the phone and on live chat with sales and support teams as part of a mystery-shopping journey.
• Rigorous by instinct. You control variables without being told to, and you notice when a result is too good to be true.
• Confident in Excel: you will be building and filling structured scoring sheets every week.
• You can write. Findings that nobody can read do not help an editor.
• Genuinely detail-obsessed: you investigate the outlier before you publish it, not after a reader emails in.
• Comfortable saying a product is bad, in writing, with evidence, when the commercial wind is blowing the other way.
• Practical AI fluency. You understand which AI techniques can increase your output, when to use them and when not to. You can demonstrate their use in your day-to-day work, not just talk about the tools: show how you build repeatable workflows, check accuracy and turn time saved into more completed testing and clearer findings. Keep improving your approach as the tools evolve, and remain accountable for everything you produce.
Nice to have
• Prior work in a testing lab, QA function, consumer reviews outlet or prod

Empire: Four Kingdoms launched in January 2013 and is the world’s all-time highest-grossing app produced by a German company. It is part of our Empire brand, which has passed €1 billion in revenue and 220 million registered players. Now we are moving the game from Adobe AIR to Unity. Quality is the heart of that move: the Unity client has to behave exactly like today’s client, 1:1, including its known quirks, while the live team keeps shipping new content every month.
We are looking for a QA Automation Engineer, Mobile Games - Freelance who builds that proof as an automated, AI-assisted test setup: automation first, AI agents for the legwork, people for the judgement calls, and no endless manual passes.
This is a senior freelance role where you work autonomously, full-time from February 2027 until the end of 2027 including handover. It is fully remote within ±3 hours of CET, with the option to meet as a team in one of our Hamburg offices.
## YOUR MISSION
• Design the test strategy and test plans for the port based on the live game, game design documents and the list of features to migrate. Prioritise by risk and agree the standards with the game’s QA lead.
• Build automated tests that run the AIR client and the Unity client side by side: same input, same result. Think replayed server traffic, state comparison and pixel diffs, where pass or fail is deterministic, not a judgement call.
• Use AI tools like Claude as a real part of your work: to generate and maintain test scripts, explore the game, cluster crashes and draft bug reports, with a human checking the result. Build tooling where it pays off, and measure whether it does.
• Perform smoke tests, sanity checks and full regression testing for every port build, and turn each new live feature and content release into regression cases for the Unity client.
• Test what players feel: payments and in-app purchases, store builds, login, push notifications, localisation, and the analytics events the business relies on, checked event by event with the data team.
• Run a device matrix on real devices, including low-end Android phones and older iPhones, and track load time, memory, frame rate, heat and battery against the live client.
• Identify, document and report defects in Jira, manage tickets and coordinate with the port team so that release deadlines are met.
• Support the release in a first market and then on all stores: release candidates, store certification, a tested rollback path and clear go or no-go input.
• Hand over a test suite and documentation that the live QA team can run and extend after the port.
## WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH
You join the port team of Empire: Four Kingdoms and report to the project lead.
• Project lead: the owner of the port, who sets priorities and is your day-to-day contact.
• The game’s QA lead: reviews your test approach and signs off quality for the Empire team.
• The port team: the Lead Unity Engineer, the Unity developers and a second QA Engineer joining later. You share test plans, review each other’s work and keep one testing standard.
• The Empire team: producers, game designers, client and server developers who know the game inside out. You involve them early and learn from them.
• Data team: to check that the tracking events from the Unity client mean the same as today.
• External QA partners: where we use them, you help coordinate their testing.
## YOUR BACKSTORY
• 6+ years of hands-on QA experience in games, with a focus on test automation and a solid understanding of the bug life cycle and testing methodologies.
• You have tested at least one live mobile game with a significant user base, through store release and live updates. This is a hard requirement.
• Hands-on mobile and game test automation, for example Appium, AltTester, GameDriver, Unity Test Framework or comparable tools, and scripting in Python, C# or a similar language, including running tests in CI.
• You work autonomously: you own your test approach, set priorities with the project lead and raise risks early, without needing day-to-day direction.
• Practical experience using AI tools (Claude, Cursor, Copilot or similar) in QA: generating and maintaining tests, triaging failures, writing tooling. You know where they help and where they don’t.
• Understanding of client-server games: you can read network traffic and tell a client bug from a server bug.
• Experience testing payments and in-app purchases on iOS and Android.
• Fluent English; you can explain complex technical issues to cross-functional teams.
## NICE TO HAVE
• Experience testing a port, migration or major rewrite against the original
• Automated visual regression testing or replay-based testing
• Building agentic tooling for QA teams. This is a real differentiator for us.
• Adobe AIR, Flash or Unity client testing
• Live mobile F2P and strategy games (live ops cadence, events, A/B tests)
• Analytics and tracking validation
• German
## WHY JOIN US?
• A classic at a turning point. You work on one of Europe’s most successful mobile strategy games at the moment it moves to a modern engine, and millions of players will feel the result.
• Work your way. Fully remote within ±3 hours of CET, with the option to meet the team in our Hamburg offices for kick-offs and key milestones.
• AI in daily work. We use AI tools like Claude every day and give you room to build the QA tooling you always wanted, judged by results.
• A team that knows the game. You build on more than a decade of knowledge in the Empire team and leave behind a test setup that lasts.
## HOW WE WILL INTERVIEW
Heads up: we will ask you to show your AI testing workflow live in the interview. Bring your real setup, your real prompts, your real failures. We care more about how you actually work than about a polished demo.
## ABOUT GOODGAME STUDIOS
Goodgame Studios is known for data-driven game development and successful live-service strategy titles. We self-publish our games in-house with all relevant disciplines under one roof. Our studio is based in Hamburg, Germany, and we welcome applications from international candidates. English is our working language. As part of Stillfront Group , one of Europe’s leading game publishers, we work on long-term IP growth with a strong focus on execution.

• Offer.

## Meet the Team
Our team is part of the Cisco AI and Automation portfolio, responsible for the "Circuit" platform—the central AI engine that powers productivity and process automation for all of Cisco. We are a rapidly expanding, high-impact group dedicated to building the vehicle for AI-driven business transformation. We operate at the intersection of applied research and production, ensuring our technology is not only cutting-edge but also optimized for performance, reliability, and functional quality for our 80,000+ monthly users.
As an Automation QA Engineer, you are the guardian of that functional quality—owning the automated testing ecosystem that keeps Circuit reliable, scalable, and production-ready across every release. This is a hybrid position.
## Your Impact
As an Automation QA Engineer , you will drive the transformation of our regression testing ecosystem, moving beyond manual processes to build AI-driven, fully automated test suites for both new and legacy features. You will design and own end-to-end (E2E), API, and performance test automation that ensures the Circuit platform continues to meet Cisco's high standards for functional quality and performance.
You will build and maintain scalable test frameworks, integrate them into CI/CD pipelines for continuous quality feedback, and leverage AI-assisted coding tools (such as Cursor, Copilot, or Claude Code) to generate and maintain tests—while rigorously validating that AI-generated artifacts are stable, correct, and compliant with security standards. This is a high-visibility role where your ability to automate functional quality and reduce technical debt directly ensures Circuit remains a reliable vehicle for process automation across Cisco.
## Responsibilities
Automated Regression & E2E Testing: Architect, build, and maintain comprehensive automated regression and end-to-end test suites for the entire Circuit platform using Playwright (TypeScript/JavaScript), Python/Pytest , and Selenium, replacing manual QA with scalable automation.
API Testing: Design and automate REST and GraphQL API test suites covering functional correctness, contract validation, error handling, and performance—including validation of AI/model-serving endpoints under concurrent load.
Performance & Load Testing: Plan and execute load, stress, and soak tests using k6 or JMeter, ; track response-time percentiles (p95/p99), throughput, error rates, and AI-specific metrics such as Time to First Token (TTFT) and inter-token latency.
AI-Driven Test Automation: Use AI agents and AI-assisted coding tools (Cursor, Copilot, Claude Code) to generate and maintain regression suites for new and legacy features; read and judge the stability of auto-generated code and ensure it does not violate security standards before it is merged.
AI Application & Agent Validation: Develop testing approaches for AI/LLM features—validating model response quality, behavior consistency (stability testing), and end-to-end AI agent workflows across both the reasoning and action layers.
CI/CD Integration & Reporting: Integrate all automated tests into CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or equivalent) for continuous validation; build dashboards and reports (Grafana, Allure) and communicate quality metrics, risk assessments, and defect trends to engineering leadership.
Cross-Functional Leadership: Act as a "Team Captain" for automation initiatives—defining standards, mentoring peers, and collaborating with development, product, and UX teams to embed automation-first testing into the core development lifecycle.
## Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor's degree with 4+ years, Master's degree with 3+ years, or PhD with 1+ year of related experience in Computer Science, AI/ML, or a related technical field.
• Experience in test automation and regression framework development , with a deep understanding of functional quality assurance.
• Experience with Playwright (TypeScript/JavaScript) for E2E/UI automation and/or Python with Pytest /Robot Framework; familiarity with Selenium.
• Experience with REST API testing (and familiarity with API contract testing); GraphQL testing a plus.
• Solid conceptual and practical knowledge of software development lifecycles, including CI/CD pipelines (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or similar) and automated testing best practices.
• Experience in AI-assisted coding tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code), critical thinking, and Agile/Git workflows to ensure high-quality, scalable test automation
## Preferred Qualifications
• Experience testing AI/ML-powered web applications , including LLM-based features, chatbots, or AI agent workflows.
• Hands-on experience with performance/load testing (k6, JMeter) and AI/LLM performance metrics (TTFT, inter-token latency, token throughput).
• Experience in AI Ops / MLOps , or building/fine-tuning custom LLMs.
• Experience with observability and reporting tools such as Splunk , Grafana, Prometheus,
• Familiarity with Docker and Kubernetes for test environment management, and with Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
• Proven track record of leading technical projects and mentoring junior engineers.
• Strong communication and collaboration skills; ability to influence cross-functional stakeholders.
• Experience building and productizing agentic applications with a focus on evaluation and business acceptance.
